subject: SCOUT: Traffic accounting & KV cache behavior for Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Priya Nair <priya@scoutai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jacob Miller <jmiller@scoutai.com>
Date: 2028-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry + sample traffic

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting close to a committed capacity conversation and need a clearer picture of how to map our traffic to a Reserved/Dedicated footprint. Attached is a sample (hourly) extraction from the last 7 days. High level:
- Product: Scout.ai inference API (text-generation + structured post-processing)
- Current peak concurrent sessions: ~250 (short spikes to ~380 during batch-run windows)
- Typical prompt size: 150-300 tokens (mostly prompts are 180 tokens median)
- Typical response: 400-900 tokens (median ~520 tokens)
- Model: currently experimenting with a mixture of open models; our production target is lower-latency small-medium models.
- Cache: we have a prefix reuse pattern for conversational threads; estimate 25-35% effective KV reuse.

Can Redwood give a ballpark reserved capacity recommendation and guidance on how KV/prefix caching changes GPU mapping? Also curious if you have guidance on burst-handling vs reserved baseline.

Appended: scout_traffic_hourly_sample.csv

Thanks,
Priya Nair
Head of Platform
ScoutAI

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry + sample traffic

Hi Priya — thanks for the sample, that helps a lot.

I've attached a short intake questionnaire to capture the specifics we need for a sizing sketch: pre-sales-scout-questionnaire.pdf. Key asks we use to translate traffic into a dedicated footprint:
- Peak sustained concurrency window (15m / 1h) and absolute spike (seconds)
- Prompt / response token distributions (p10/p50/p90), and proportion of requests that hit the cache
- Session affinity requirement (are sessions sticky to GPUs / do you require KV persistence tied to session?)
- Target p95 latency SLO and acceptable tail (e.g., 95th 500ms generator-only)
- Workload mix by model family (short vs long responses; reranking/embedding/offline)

If you can fill the PDF and return the CSV with a 24-hr busy-day extraction (preferred), we can do a quick back-of-envelope that maps to GPU SKUs and suggested reserved commit. I've looped in Vivek (serving/runtime) and Ben (sales) for an expedited estimate.

Two quick notes:
- KV/prefix cache reuse is one of the highest-leverage levers: a 30% effective hit rate typically reduces total token compute by ~20–25% for generation-heavy workloads, but it has small impact on peak concurrency (because cache benefits are per-token).
- For burst handling we typically recommend a committed baseline sized to a 95th-day profile plus a small burst pool (managed via autoscaling/overprovision burst credits) — we'll sketch numbers once we have the questionnaire.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Attachment: pre-sales-scout-questionnaire.pdf

- Absolute short spike (observed over last 7d): 380 (typically during nightly summary batch kickoffs, lasts ~3–5 mins)

Team — quick read: Scout provided a 7-day extract and inline answers (see Jacob's email). High level numbers: 270 15m conc, 380 short spikes, median prompt ~180, median response ~520, KV reuse ~30%. They want a Reserved/Dedicated recommendation + burst strategy.

Specific asks for sizing calc:
1) Convert token profile to token-ops per second at peak (use p95 window 15m = 270 conc * mean tokens per request).
2) Estimate GPU token throughput per SKU for our low-latency small-medium model profile (prefer H100-optimized kernels). Suggest SKU mix and count for a 95th-day baseline and a burst buffer.
3) Estimate the impact of 30% KV hits on aggregate token compute and whether session-affinity (30–60m) requires pinning KV to the same node or a distributed KV approach.

Vivek — can you run a quick EBC (back-of-envelope) by EOD? Ben/Laura — once we have counts I'll draft a committed proposal with suggested burst credits and an intro to contract terms.

Thanks — Vanessa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-06T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: SCOUT quick EBC + questions before we send a sketch

Vanessa — quick EBC notes below (assumptions listed):
Assumptions:
- Model class: small-medium tuned generation ~ 35M-70M params equivalent with optimized kernels (throughput ~ 5k–8k tokens/sec per H100 for short sequences, conservative).
- Use 1h sustained peak window for sizing to avoid oscillation.
- Average tokens per request during peak = prompt(200) + response(600) = 800 tokens (close to Jacob's medians).
- Effective KV reduction: 30% token compute saved across generation tokens only (not forwarding overhead).

Calculations:
- Concurrency 270 reqs over 15m window => approximate RPS = 270 / (avg request duration in seconds). For sizing we use token-driven throughput: 270 concurrent * 800 tokens = 216k live tokens in-flight snapshot. If we assume an average per-request generation pacing that maps to ~2s effective generation window that yields ~135k tokens/sec sustained at that moment.
- After 30% KV reuse: token compute ~95k tokens/sec equivalent.
- Per-H100 conservative throughput: 7k tokens/sec => required H100-equivalent GPUs = 95k / 7k ≈ 14 H100 GPUs for baseline 95th profile.
- To handle short spikes to ~380 (40% higher), add a small burst pool or autoscale headroom: 14 * 1.4 ≈ 20 H100-equivalents peak.

Practical recommendation:
- Recommended reserved commit: 14 H100-equivalents (or comparable lower-SKU equivalent) as Dedicated baseline to cover 95th profile.
- Add a burst reserve of 6 GPUs (or use reserved baseline + autoscale credits that allow spiking to 20) for nightly summary windows.
- KV/prefix behavior: keep KV in a shared high-availability distributed KV (not strictly pinned) to avoid wasted node-resources; session-affinity for short-lived stickiness (30–60m) can be handled via consistent routing with cache replication for hot keys — this avoids having to overcommit GPUs for KV residency.

Attachments: ebc_back_of_envelope.xlsx (workbook with the token math and alternative SKU mappings)

I'll hand off to Ben to translate into committed units and Laura to check contract terms for burst credits and SLA.

— Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SCOUT: Traffic accounting & KV cache behavior for Dedicated commit — next steps

Priya / Jacob — thanks for the fast turnaround and for sharing the extract. Summary and next steps: 

Summary (short):
- Preliminary sizing: ~14 H100-equivalent GPUs to cover a 95th-day sustained baseline given your token profile and ~30% KV reuse.
- Burst handling: factor ~1.4 headroom -> reserve a 6-GPU burst pool (sketching peak to ~20 H100-equivalents) or use autoscale credits to cover short 3–5 minute spikes.
- KV approach: recommend distributed KV with operational replication for hot keys and consistent routing to preserve session affinity without strict node pinning.

Next steps:
1) Priya/Jacob: please confirm whether 30% KV reuse is accurate across the busiest user cohorts; if it's higher we can reduce baseline further.
2) We'll schedule a 60-minute technical sizing workshop (Vivek + 1 engineer) to walk the sample CSV and finalize recommendations — propose Tue 2028-09-12 or Wed 2028-09-13. Please pick a slot.
3) Ben/Laura will follow with a draft committed proposal that shows: (a) 14 H100-equivalents baseline pricing, (b) burst buffer pricing/credit model, and (c) SLA language re: latency targets.

I attached the workbook Vivek used for the EBC so you can see the token math.

Thanks again — we aim to get a scoped committed recommendation within 48 hours of the workshop.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
